The role that owns `<schema>.<table>` (`pg_tables.tableowner`) -- that role implicitly holds every privilege on the table (INSERT, SELECT, ...) without ever appearing as a `grantee` row for a real GRANT, which is exactly the shape `_roles_with_table_privilege` above reads.

Used below to keep that owner (the migration-running operator role, e.g. `mitatedbsvc_provision`) from being misidentified as matching every platform-plane role class at once (M-1, WP-4 integration review 2026-09-10, peer-symmetric with r2db-api's own `_table_owner`).

Returns `None` if the table does not exist (a caller scoped to `role_classes={"api"}` or similar, e.g. `mitatedb_api.main`'s own startup F-16 call, may run before `0005_application_audit.sql` is guaranteed applied against the connection it happens to be given) -- exactly like `_roles_with_table_privilege` above, which already tolerates a missing table by simply returning no rows.
`None` never equals a real role name, so the exclusion checks below simply never match in that case, the same as if this function were never called at all.
